title: The Pair of Hoopoes and the Treasure
logline: A poor servant spends his whole wages, two dinars, to keep a pair of caged hoopoes together and set them free; the birds repay him with a buried jar of gold, and even the king lets him keep it.
moral: Kindness given without counting the cost comes back multiplied; and when destiny arrives, even obvious things can be hidden from the sharpest eyes.
tone: Warm and gentle with light comedy: a small man with a big heart, two fragile birds, one quiet piece of wisdom. Suspense only in the market; no villainy played for fear.

beats.summary: The servant decides to leave his job and travel.
Two dinars: all his wages. One for charity, one for food.
Two weak hoopoes in one cage.
One dinar is refused: both birds cost everything he has.
They may be a pair; buying one would tear them apart.
He pays both dinars and keeps nothing.
Not here: another hunter could catch them.
Far away among the trees he opens the cage gently.
The birds decide to reward him: a jar of gold lies under the tree.
His question: you saw buried gold but not the net?
When destiny arrives, obvious things can be hidden from the eyes.
The clay jar is full of gold dinars.
The king refuses the gold: keep it, it is yours.
He leaves with the gold, remembering the two birds.

sets.description: Planned marketStreet, palette clear (daylight). Three places on it: the merchant house door at x 220..360 (S1, S2); the market end with two striped awnings, a crate and a mat at x 560..800 and a house corner at x 60..150 (S3 to S7); the palace facade with a door at x 300..420, two steps and a balcony window at y 380 (S16). Ground y 900. Bake one layer per place.

Planned countryRoad: a 2400-unit strip, ground y 900, with the city edge at the left end, a milestone at x 1100, hills (Library hillTrees) and a tree row (Library treeRow) rising toward the right end. Only the tree hiding place and milestone are needed here.

Composed from Library pieces: sky (day), sun at (180, 150), hillTrees, treeRow with hmin 360 (many trees), ground at y 900 with the soil below drawn down to y 1230, bush at x 120. The fruit tree is Library tree(ctx, 700, 900, {w: 110, top: 330, crowns: [[700,250,170],[570,330,120],[830,330,120],[700,150,110]]}) plus a branch on the left from (700, 520) to (430, 520), 26 thick, tapering, and 8 Library figs hanging in the crown. Coordinates are a design target; adjust after a still. Buried jar centred at (640, 1050).

Planned palaceHall: arched interior, window light, tiled floor at y 900, dais (top y 860, x 620..900) with a throne (seat y 800). Added for this story: a heavy treasury door on the back wall at x 80..230, y 560..900, with a round coin emblem and a big lock.

props.description: birdCage: domed wire cage 170 wide x 200 tall at s 1 (flat base 14 thick in brown, 9 vertical bars, 2 hoops, a ring on top, a hinged door 60 x 90 on the front with angle field door 0..1.9 rad, a small seed dish inside). Drawn in two passes (back bars, then the birds, then front bars) so the birds are inside it.

The planned hangingJar drawing without the rope (clay body 130 x 150, 60 wide neck, rim, two ear handles, terracotta with red dot shading) with added fields: lid (a flat cap with a knob, lidOff 0..1), fill 0..1 (gold coins as stacked yellow ellipses at the mouth), cutaway 0..1 (front wall transparent to show the coins), tilt, soil 0..1 (dirt smears).
The planned coin / coinPile drawing: yellow disc r 16 with a black rim, an inner ring and one glint; can stand, lie (ellipse) and roll.
The planned bindle: a red dotted bundle (r 34) tied on a stick 150 long, carried on the shoulder.
The planned broom: stick 190 long with a yellow straw head 50 x 60.
The planned fishingNet mesh used as a bird net: handNet (hoop r 45 on a pole) for hunter2, a folded bundle on the hunter's shoulder, and a flat or closed net inside the thought cloud.
Library fig, r 14, eight hanging in the crown of the fruit tree.
Library heart: between the caged pair (r 24), drifting down as thanks, in the last cloud.

subtitles.ar: كان رجل يعمل خادمًا عند أحد الأغنياء،|ثم قرر أن يترك عمله ويسافر.|أعطاه صاحب العمل دينارين أجرًا له.|أراد الرجل أن يتصدق بدينار، وأن يحتفظ بالآخر لطعامه في الطريق.
subtitles.en: A man worked as a servant for a wealthy person,|then decided to leave his job and travel.|His employer gave him two dinars in wages.|The man wanted to give one dinar in charity and keep the other for food on the road.

subtitles.ar: دخل السوق فرأى صيادًا يبيع هدهدين ضعيفين في قفص واحد.|سأل عن ثمنهما، فقال الصياد: «ديناران.»|حاول أن يشتريهما بدينار واحد،|لكن الصياد رفض.
subtitles.en: He entered the market and saw a hunter selling two weak hoopoes in one cage.|He asked their price, and the hunter said, “Two dinars.”|He tried to buy both for one dinar,|but the hunter refused.

subtitles.ar: فكر الرجل أن يشتري طائرًا واحدًا ويترك الآخر.|ثم خاف أن يكون الهدهدان زوجين، وأن يفرقهما عن بعضهما.|أشفق عليهما، ودفع الدينارين معًا،|ولم يبقَ معه شيء من أجره.
subtitles.en: The man considered buying one bird and leaving the other.|Then he feared they might be a pair and he would separate them.|He felt compassion, paid both dinars,|and had none of his wages left.

subtitles.ar: لم يرد أن يطلق الطائرين وسط السوق؛|فقد كانا جائعين وضعيفين، وربما أمسك بهما صياد آخر.|سار بهما إلى أرض بعيدة فيها أشجار كثيرة،|وفتح القفص برفق.
subtitles.en: He did not want to release the birds in the market:|they were hungry and weak, and another hunter might catch them.|He walked to a distant place full of trees|and gently opened the cage.

subtitles.ar: طار الهدهدان بصعوبة حتى وصلا إلى شجرة مثمرة.|جلسا فوق غصن، وشكرا الرجل لأنه أنقذهما.|ثم قال أحدهما للآخر: «علينا أن نكافئه.|تحت هذه الشجرة جرّة مليئة بالذهب.»
subtitles.en: The two hoopoes flew with difficulty to a fruit tree.|They perched on a branch and thanked the man for rescuing them.|Then one said to the other, “We must reward him.|Beneath this tree is a jar full of gold.”

subtitles.ar: سمع الرجل كلامهما ودهش. سألهما: «كيف عرفتما مكان ذهب مخفي تحت الأرض،|ولم تريا شبكة الصياد التي أمسكت بكما؟»|أجاب أحد الهدهدين: «حين يأتي القدر،|قد تغيب عن العيون أشياء واضحة.»
subtitles.en: The man heard them and was astonished. He asked, “How did you know about gold hidden underground,|yet fail to see the hunter’s net that caught you?”|One hoopoe answered, “When destiny arrives,|even obvious things may be hidden from our eyes.”

subtitles.ar: حفر الرجل عند أصل الشجرة، حتى وجد جرّة من الفخار.|فتحها، فإذا هي مليئة بالدنانير الذهبية.|شكر الهدهدين ودعا لهما بالسلامة،|ثم حمل الكنز وعاد به.
subtitles.en: The man dug beside the tree until he found a clay jar.|He opened it and discovered it was full of gold dinars.|He thanked the two hoopoes and wished them well,|then carried the treasure away.

subtitles.ar: وبعد وقت، أخبر الرجل ملك البلاد بما حدث،|وعرض أن يضع الذهب في خزينة القصر.|لكن الملك قال له: «احتفظ به، فهو لك.»|فخرج الرجل من عند الملك والذهب معه، يتذكر الطائرين.
subtitles.en: Later the man told the king what had happened|and offered to place the gold in the royal treasury.|But the king said, “Keep it. It belongs to you.”|The man left the king carrying the gold, remembering the two birds.

new_assets.name: hoopoe (bird kind)
new_assets.description: A new kind 'hoopoe' on the Library bird with two palettes (pal 0 cinnamon, pal 1 pale peach, 8 % smaller): barred black and white wing and tail, long thin curved beak, and a fan crest of 6 or 7 black-tipped feathers driven by the existing crest field (0 folded back, 1 fully fanned).
new_assets.implementation: Add BIRD.hoopoe colours; draw the wing as the existing wing shape in black with three white bar polygons clipped to it; beak as a quadratic curve stroked 5 wide tapering to a point; crest as N tapered triangles rotated about the crown from -0.2 rad (folded) to a fan of 1.4 rad, each with a black tip. Default look of other kinds unchanged; run the regression test.

new_assets.name: person costume presets (hunter)
new_assets.description: Adds a 'hunter' (fowler) preset to the planned person costume layer: skull cap with a feather, stubble, sleeveless jerkin, optional net on the shoulder; palette option for a second hunter. This film also uses the planned presets 'servant', 'richMan' and 'king'.
new_assets.implementation: Same body, face, arm IK and PERSON_HANDS as every preset; headwear and jerkin as flat shapes over the torso; stubble as 8 dots; the net bundle is the fishingNet mesh clipped to a rounded blob.

new_assets.name: birdCage
new_assets.description: Domed wire cage 170 x 200 with a hinged door (door 0..1.9 rad), carry ring, seed dish; back and front bar passes so characters sit inside. Reusable for any caged bird or small animal.
new_assets.implementation: cageBack(ctx, x, y, P) and cageFront(ctx, x, y, P): base rect, bars as lines to an arc dome, two hoops as ellipses; the door is a small barred rect rotated about its hinge with a horizontal squeeze (cos of the angle).

new_assets.name: hangingJar
new_assets.description: Uses the planned clay jar drawing standing on the ground, with new fields lidOff, fill (gold), cutaway, tilt and soil, so one jar serves as buried treasure and as a hanging store jar.
new_assets.implementation: Rope drawn only when a hook is given. Coins at the mouth are 5 to 7 yellow ellipses; cutaway fills the body silhouette with soil colour at alpha and draws 4 rows of coin ellipses inside the clip.

new_assets.name: stick, coinPile, smallBowl
new_assets.description: Uses the planned coin / coinPile drawing for the two dinars, the spilled coins and the jar fill; this film adds stand, lie and roll states for a single coin.
new_assets.implementation: Disc r 16 with rim and inner ring; lying = ellipse with a 4 px edge; rolling angle = distance / r.

new_assets.name: fishingNet
new_assets.description: Uses the planned mesh drawing as a bird net: hand net, folded bundle, flat net and closed bag (in the thought cloud).
new_assets.implementation: Diamond mesh lines clipped to the given outline (hoop, blob, flat ellipse, bag).

new_assets.name: groundWindow
new_assets.description: A round see-through window into the earth (r up to 130) that irises open at a point below ground level to show what is buried: darker soil, pebbles, root tips and whatever is drawn inside. Reusable for buried treasure, burrows, seeds, hidden water.
new_assets.implementation: ctx.save(); arc clip at (x, y, r(t)); fill the darker soil with red Ben-Day dots, 6 seeded pebbles, 2 root curves; call the inside-draw callback; restore; stroke a dashed black rim 6 wide. Radius eased with a 10 % overshoot.

new_assets.name: goldGlow
new_assets.description: Treasure light: 9 tapering yellow rays fanning up from a point with a yellow halftone disc behind and 3 staggered star glints; strength 0..1.
new_assets.implementation: Rays as thin triangles with seeded lengths that breathe 5 %; halftone disc from the style module; glints with the K star primitive on offsets of 0.2 s.

new_assets.name: thoughtCloud
new_assets.description: The planned generic thought cloud, used four times: the two-coin plan (S2), buying one bird (S5), the net (S11, S12) and the remembered birds (S16).
new_assets.implementation: thoughtCloud(ctx, box, t, drawInside): scalloped white cloud with a black brush outline, three trail bubbles toward the thinker, a clip, then the inside draw at its own scale.

new_assets.name: weakFlight
new_assets.description: A struggling flight path for small birds: from A to B in n sagging arcs, each ending higher, with a short hover between, flap rate rising at the bottom of each arc; returns x, y, flap, rot, sq. The strong flight later uses a plain arc for contrast. (The guide lists flight(t, path, mood) as wanted; this is its weak mood.)
new_assets.implementation: Piecewise quadratic beziers between keyed points; y adds a downward sine sag per segment; flap = 1 + 0.5 * sag depth; rot from the path tangent; pure function of t.

new_assets.name: person kneel / sit
new_assets.description: Uses the planned kneel and sit fields (man kneeling to open the cage and to dig; king seated on the throne and rising). Adds a dig cycle: while kneeling the two arms alternate between a reach into the hole and a throw back.
new_assets.implementation: dig(t, t0, rate) returns handL/handR targets on two half-phase-shifted ellipses (reach down-forward, sweep back-up) for the arm IK, plus a small torso bob; dirt clods are spawned from K.rng on each throw.

new_assets.name: marketStreet
new_assets.description: Uses the planned street in the clear palette at three places (merchant door, market corner with awnings, palace facade with steps and balcony).
new_assets.implementation: As planned; this film adds two striped awnings, a crate, a mat and two palace steps as separate small drawings on top of the baked layer.

new_assets.name: countryRoad
new_assets.description: Uses the planned road strip for one 5 s tracking walk from the city edge to the trees.
new_assets.implementation: Three parallax layers baked wide: skyline and hills (0.3), tree row (0.6), road with milestone (1.0).

new_assets.name: palaceHall (variant merchantHouse)
new_assets.description: Uses the planned palace hall with a throne on the dais and adds a treasury door (coin emblem, lock) on the back wall.
new_assets.implementation: As planned; the treasury door is a rounded rect in brown with two iron bands, a yellow coin disc and a black lock.

owner_questions: A second hunter is shown for 1.5 s as an eye and a hand net peeking round a corner to picture the words "another hunter might catch them"; default: keep it (it is the man's worry made visible, not an event added to the story).
The man overhears the hoopoes because he has turned to pick up the cage, and the buried jar is shown to the audience through a round ground window as the bird speaks; default: keep both.
The fruit tree is drawn as a fig tree (the script says only "a fruit tree") to reuse the Library fig; default: fig tree.
Charity is shown in a thought cloud as a coin landing in an open hand with a heart, with no beggar character; default: no beggar.

Invented English lettering beyond the script: THE SERVANT, 2 HOOPOES, 2 DINARS!, 1?, NO!, A PAIR?, DINARS: 0, FAR AWAY, FLAP! FLAP!, PSST..., JAR, CLINK!, CLAY JAR, TREASURY, KEEP IT!; default: keep all, they are short and each sits on its spoken word.
At the end two real hoopoes fly over the man and land near him while he remembers them (the script says only that he remembers the two birds); default: keep the fly-over, he waves.
The second hoopoe (the smaller, quieter one) speaks the moral, while the first proposes the reward; the script says only "one of them"; default: as described.
The hunter bites a coin and the man holds up two fingers at the open jar (small comic touches); default: keep both.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; cue every action with w(p, n) from timing.json. The times in this plan are the word starts in planning/inputs/timeline.md; do not re-estimate.
Set LIFE.t = t each frame so every character blinks; add hand blinks where a lid is set explicitly. Give every character a gaze target at all times (look() / lookAt()).

Hoopoes are the Library bird with the new kind: use crest as their main emotion channel (0 flat = weak, afraid, caught out; 0.3 to 0.5 = interest; 1 = thanks, joy, the moral). Talking = beak flutter between 1 and 1.3 on the speaker only; the listener tilts headRot.
The pair never moves in unison: hoopoeB follows hoopoeA by 3 to 6 frames (stagger) except in S12, where she leads.
